sources.title: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both

research_question: Does the direction of the early UTC trading block predict the direction of the following equal-length block across liquid crypto perpetuals?
hypothesis: Delayed information diffusion and intraday liquidity provision create time-series continuation from an early daily return block into the following block.
source_deviation: The papers study specific hourly/half-hour return pairs, largely on BTC and a few majors. This preregistered broad-universe adaptation uses equal early/following UTC blocks and fixed block lengths, with one-hour delayed execution after the signal block to avoid same-boundary fills.
universe_rule: Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals listed by 2021-12-31; each day retain the top 30 contemporaneously eligible contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume.
signal: At UTC hour H, use return from 00:00 UTC open through the close of hour H-1. Position direction for each asset is sign(signal).
execution: Execute at H+1 UTC open, one full hour after signal completion; exit H hours later. Equal absolute weights across top-30 assets, gross exposure 1.0. Portfolio is flat outside the holding block.
cost_model: Charge entry plus exit cost each day (2 x gross exposure x one-way bps).
development_gate: Canonical net daily-equity Sharpe >0.70, canonical total return >0, at least 2/3 block lengths positive, and both development years non-negative.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; positive at 2x costs; >=2/3 block lengths positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; an additional one-hour execution delay remains positive; DSR reported.
